prompt: The Dataverse connector supports four triggers. Match each trigger to when it starts a flow.

left.text: When a row is added, modified or deleted
When a flow step is run from a business process flow

right.text: A row is added, modified, or deleted in a Dataverse table
A Dataverse action completes, such as a custom business event
Someone selects the Run Flow button in a business process flow step
A user in a model-driven app selects a row and runs the flow

explanation: Die vier Dataverse-Trigger decken unterschiedliche Ereignisquellen ab: Datenzeilen-Änderungen, abgeschlossene Dataverse-Aktionen (z. B. ein selbst definiertes Ereignis wie EmployeeOnboarded), den Run-Flow-Schritt eines Business Process Flow und die manuelle Auswahl einer Zeile in einer modellgesteuerten App.

source.title: Dataverse triggers
source.quote: When a row is added, modified or deleted - Use this trigger to start a flow when a row is added, modified, or deleted in a Dataverse table. When an action is performed - This trigger occurs when a Dataverse action completes. When a flow step is run from a business process flow - With this trigger, you can start a flow when someone selects the Run Flow button in a business process flow step. When a row is selected - This trigger starts a flow when a user in a Power Apps model-driven app selects a row and runs the flow.

prompt: Match each scope option of the "When a row is added, modified or deleted" trigger to what it means.

right.text: The default — any user who owns a row and modifies it can trigger the flow
The most limiting — the flow only runs if you own the modified row
Triggers if anyone in your business unit owns the modified row
Also includes users of any child business units

explanation: Der Scope legt fest, wessen Datensatzbesitz den Flow auslösen darf. Organization ist der Standard und am weitesten, User am engsten. Business Unit und Parent:Child Business Unit liegen dazwischen. Bei organisationseigenen Tabellen ist Organization die einzige Option.

source.title: Dataverse triggers
source.quote: Organization - This option is the default. Any user who owns a row and modifies it can trigger your flow. User - This option is the most limiting; your flow only runs if you own the modified row. Business Unit - This option triggers your flow if anyone in your business unit owns the modified row. Parent: Child Business Unit - This option includes any child business unit users in determining whose actions can trigger your flow.

prompt: A flow triggers on modified rows and later uses an update row action to update columns on the same row. How do you avoid an infinite loop?

options.text: Exclude the columns the flow updates from the trigger's Select columns option
Set the trigger scope to Organization so the flow's own updates are ignored
Add a Filter rows expression that excludes rows modified by the flow owner
Add a Terminate action after the update so the run ends before retriggering

explanation: Die Option „Select columns“ begrenzt, welche Spaltenänderungen den Flow starten. Aktualisiert der Flow später Spalten derselben Zeile, dürfen genau diese Spalten nicht in Select columns stehen — sonst löst die eigene Aktualisierung den Flow erneut aus. Achtung: Lookup-Spalten werden im Select-columns-Filter nicht unterstützt.

source.title: Dataverse triggers
source.quote: It's also important to use this feature if your flow intends to use an update row action later to update columns on the row that triggered the flow. To avoid an infinite loop, make sure that you don't include the columns that you update in the Select columns option.

prompt: A flow creates follow-up tasks whenever a Project row is added, and the tasks should show the person who created the project as their creator. The maker sets Run as to Modifying user and enables Use invoker's connection on the action, but the flow fails with a privilege error. What is missing?

options.text: The flow owner lacks the Act on Behalf of Another User privilege, found in the Delegate role
The flow owner lacks the Assign privilege on the Task table needed to transfer ownership
The modifying user must be added as a co-owner of the flow before the option works
The trigger scope must be set to User so the invoker's context is available to actions

explanation: „Run as“ lässt Dataverse-Aktionen im Kontext eines anderen Nutzers laufen. Dafür braucht der Flow-Besitzer das Privileg „Act on Behalf of Another User“ — standardmäßig in der Rolle Delegate enthalten, aber jeder Rolle hinzufügbar. Assign, Co-Ownership und der Trigger-Scope spielen dafür keine Rolle.

source.title: Dataverse triggers
source.quote: The flow owner must have the Act on Behalf of Another User Dataverse privilege. The Delegate security role includes this privilege by default, but you can add it to any security role.

prompt: By default, how many rows does the Dataverse List rows action return, and what happens when that limit is reached?

options.text: 5,000 rows, and reaching the limit silently returns incomplete data without an error
100,000 rows, and reaching the limit fails the action with a pagination error
500 rows, and reaching the limit makes the flow retry the action automatically
There is no default limit; all matching rows are returned in a single page

explanation: List rows liefert standardmäßig höchstens 5.000 Zeilen. Kritisch: Das Erreichen der Grenze wirft keinen Fehler — man bekommt einfach nicht alle Daten. Über die Einstellung Pagination lassen sich bis zu 100.000 Zeilen pro Seite abrufen; mehrere Seiten muss der Flow dann selbst per Paging-Token abarbeiten.

source.title: Query data
source.quote: By default, the action doesn't return more than 5,000 rows. You can turn on the Pagination feature from the Settings tab if you need to return more data. When you turn on pagination, you can specify a page size of up to 100,000 rows. Make sure that you consider your future needs because reaching 5,000 rows doesn't produce an error.

prompt: When you set the Select columns option on a Dataverse retrieve action, which column name must you use?

options.text: The column's logical name, listed under the column's Advanced options
The column's display name exactly as it appears on the main form and in views
The column's schema name with the publisher prefix written in upper case
The column's GUID, copied from the column properties pane in the maker portal

explanation: Für Select columns wird der logische Spaltenname gebraucht — zu finden im Abschnitt Advanced options der Spalteneigenschaften, z. B. „firstname,lastname“. Die Angabe begrenzt auch, welche Spalten später als Dynamic Content auftauchen: Fehlt eine erwartete Spalte, lohnt der Blick auf diese Option.

source.title: Query data
source.quote: Make sure that you use the table column logical name, which you can find on the Advanced options section of the column properties.

prompt: A flow pauses for an approval step that may take days. Why might you add a "Get a row by ID" action after the approval completes?

options.text: To reload the latest data so the flow doesn't act on stale values
To reset the trigger so the flow can run again for the same row after approval
To release the approval lock that Dataverse places on the record during review
To convert the pending row into an agent flow task for review by the manager

explanation: Nach einer mehrtägigen Genehmigungspause können die ursprünglich gelesenen Daten veraltet sein. Ein erneutes „Get a row by ID“ holt den aktuellen Stand und verhindert, dass der Flow auf Basis alter Werte handelt. Ist die Zeilen-ID möglicherweise null, sollte man vorher eine Bedingung prüfen — sonst schlägt der Schritt fehl.

source.title: Query data
source.quote: You might want to use the Get a row by ID action to get the latest data after the approval happens. This approach would prevent your flow from taking action based on stale data.

prompt: An approval flow follows a predictable three-part pattern. Place the parts in the correct order.

items.text: The flow sends an approval request and waits for a response
A condition routes the outcome down the right branch

explanation: Erst löst ein Trigger aus, dann sendet „Start and wait for an approval“ die Anfrage und pausiert den Flow, und schließlich liest eine Condition den Outcome (Approve/Reject) und verzweigt: True-Zweig für Genehmigungen, False-Zweig für Ablehnungen.

source.title: Build an approval request
source.quote: An approval flow follows a predictable three-part pattern: a trigger fires, the flow sends an approval request and waits for a response, and then a condition routes the outcome down the right branch.

prompt: When the "Start and wait for an approval" action runs, where does Power Automate notify the people in the Assigned to field?

options.text: By email, in the Approvals center, and optionally in Microsoft Teams
By email and in the Power Automate mobile app as push notifications, without Teams
In the Approvals center and in the Power Automate mobile app
Through a Power Apps canvas app notification and by email

explanation: Die Aktion benachrichtigt alle im Feld „Assigned to“ per E-Mail, im Approvals-Center von Power Automate und optional in Microsoft Teams. Danach pausiert der Flow, bis die nötigen Antworten vorliegen; anschließend steht der Outcome als Dynamic Content bereit.

source.title: Build an approval request
source.quote: When it runs, Power Automate sends a notification to everyone in the Assigned to field — by email, in the Power Automate Approvals center, and optionally in Microsoft Teams. The flow then pauses until the required responses arrive.

prompt: For each of the following statements about converting a cloud flow to an agent flow, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: Converting a flow to an agent flow is a one-way operation that can't be reversed.
The flow must be in a solution before it can be converted.
Agent flows consume Power Automate capacity, just like cloud flows.

explanation: Die Umwandlung ist einseitig, weil sich die Abrechnung von Power Automate auf Copilot Studio verschiebt. Voraussetzungen: Es muss ein Cloud-Flow (kein Desktop-Flow) sein, er muss in einer Solution liegen, und die Umgebung braucht Copilot-Studio-Kapazität. Agent Flows verbrauchen entsprechend Copilot-Studio- statt Power-Automate-Kapazität.

source.title: Convert a flow to an agent flow
source.quote: Converting a flow to an agent flow is a one-way operation. It can't be reversed because the flow's billing changes from Power Automate to Copilot Studio. The flow is in a solution. Consumes Copilot Studio capacity rather than Power Automate capacity.

prompt: Which agent flow activity does NOT consume Copilot Studio capacity?

options.text: Testing the flow in the designer or from an agent's test chat
Actions the flow executes when triggered in a production environment
Actions the flow executes when an autonomous agent triggers it
Actions the flow executes when triggered from a Copilot Studio conversation

explanation: Jede ausgeführte Aktion eines Agent Flow verbraucht Copilot-Studio-Kapazität — Tests im Designer oder aus dem Test-Chat eines Agents jedoch nicht. Ist die vorausbezahlte Kapazität aufgebraucht, werden neue Agent-Flow-Läufe blockiert, bis wieder Kapazität verfügbar ist.

source.title: Convert a flow to an agent flow
source.quote: Every action your agent flow executes consumes Copilot Studio capacity. Testing the flow in the designer or from an agent's test chat doesn't consume capacity.

prompt: Match each flow failure symptom to its cause and fix.

left.text: "Bad request" or "Not found", error code 400 or 404

right.text: An authentication error — usually fixed by updating the connection
An action configuration issue — edit the flow definition and resubmit
A temporary or transient failure — select Resubmit

explanation: 401/403 deuten auf Authentifizierung — Verbindung reparieren („Fix connection“) und den Lauf erneut senden. 400/404 stehen für falsch konfigurierte Aktionen: Flow bearbeiten, speichern, erneut senden. 500/502 sind vorübergehende Störungen; hier genügt Resubmit.

source.title: Troubleshoot flows
source.quote: If this type of error occurs, the error message includes the word "Unauthorized," or an error code of 401 or 403 appears. You can usually fix authentication errors by updating the connection. In this case, the error message includes the phrase "Bad request" or "Not found," or an error code 400 or 404 appears. If error code 500 or 502 appears, the failure is temporary or transient.

prompt: Why is using the trigger's Filter rows option preferable to adding a condition check in the flow's actions?

options.text: The flow only runs when the OData expression is true, which is more efficient
Filter rows supports FetchXML, while a Condition action supports OData filters alone
Filter rows is the only place where lookup columns can be used in a filter
A Condition action can't reference the trigger's Dataverse outputs directly

explanation: Mit „Filter rows“ und einem OData-Ausdruck startet der Flow nur, wenn die Bedingung nach dem Speichern in Dataverse wahr ist. Eine Bedingungsprüfung in den Aktionen erreicht dasselbe Ergebnis, ist aber weniger effizient, weil der Flow trotzdem für jede Änderung anläuft.

source.title: Dataverse triggers
source.quote: While adding a condition check to your flow actions could accomplish the same task, it's less efficient than using a filter rows expression. The flow runs only when the system evaluates the expression to be true after you save the change in Dataverse.

prompt: Complete the statement about retrieving related table data in a Dataverse action.
textParts: By default, retrieve data actions only retrieve data from the primary table. Use the
option with an OData-style expression to include data from related tables — but the related columns don't appear in the
pane, so you need a workflow expression to access them.

options.text: Expand Query
Select columns
Filter rows
Dynamic content
Settings
Run history

explanation: Expand Query (unter Advanced parameters) holt per OData-Ausdruck wie primarycontactid($select=contactid,fullname) Daten verknüpfter Tabellen mit. Diese Spalten erscheinen aber nicht im Dynamic-Content-Bereich — der Zugriff erfolgt über einen Workflow-Ausdruck.

source.title: Query data
source.quote: You can use the Expand Query option to provide an OData-style expression to include data from related tables. While this expression includes data in the output of the actions, it doesn't include the data columns in the Dynamic content pane for selection. To use the related data, you need to use a workflow expression to access the data.

prompt: A flow triggers on multiple change types and needs conditional logic depending on which one occurred. Which expression returns the change type, and what values does it contain?

options.text: triggerBody()?['SdkMessage'] — it contains Create, Update, or Delete
triggerOutputs()?['ChangeType'] — it contains Added, Modified, or Removed
body('Trigger')?['Operation'] — it contains Insert, Edit, or Drop
variables('changeType') — it must be set manually

explanation: Der Ausdruck triggerBody()?['SdkMessage'] liefert den auslösenden Änderungstyp; die Eigenschaft SdkMessage enthält Create, Update oder Delete. Wichtig außerdem: Bei mehreren Aktualisierungen derselben Zeile kann der Flow mehrfach starten, auch wenn sich Werte nicht ändern — die Flow-Logik muss das berücksichtigen.

source.title: Dataverse triggers
source.quote: If you trigger your flow on multiple change types, and if you need conditional logic depending on the type, then you can use the following expression to get the change type that triggered the flow. The SdkMessage property contains Create, Update, or Delete.
